docs.title: 3. Initialize TaskHopper
docs.text:
Now that TaskHopper is installed, it is time to initialize the CLI. (this is a one-time command)

hop init

docs.title: Validate Installation
docs.text:
> hop -h

Should produce the following output:

usage: hop [-h]  ...

positional arguments:

    carrot    perform carrot action
    foo       It says the thing
    docs      open ~/repos/cordata/dev-docs/_asse...
    test_it   echo 'it works'
    current   show current project details
    list      list configured projects
    to        cd to project directory

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

docs.title: What does init do?
docs.text:
• Sets up required directories (located at ~/.hop)
  • Checks that python3 is installed and creates a virtual environment for dependencies
  • Installs python dependencies into the virtual environment

* You can rerun init to clear the existing init by passing the -f flag

docs.title: Sample .hoprc
docs.text:
This sample config will add an alias test for the command echo 'It Works!'

# ~/.hoprc
commands:
  test: echo 'It works!'

docs.title: Test it out
docs.text:
View the help:

> hop -h
usage: hop [-h]  ...

positional arguments:

    carrot    perform carrot action
    test      echo 'It works!'

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

Run the command:

> hop test
It works!

docs.title: View available carrots
docs.text:
> hop carrot available
Available Carrots
-----------------

project_manager

docs.title: Install the Project Manager Carrot
docs.text:
> hop carrot install project_manager

Check for the new commands:

> hop -h
usage: hop [-h]  ...

positional arguments:
    carrot    perform carrot action
    test      echo 'It works!'
    current   show current project details
    list      list configured projects
    to        cd to project directory

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

Thats it! You are ready to go! Explore the documentation to learn how to use Task Hopper to its fullest extent.
